meetings.headline: Stormwater Task Force reviewed town MS4 compliance; catch basin cleaning, training and funding gaps flagged, no membership expansion.
meetings.summary: The Stormwater Task Force met with its consultant CEI to review the town's MS4 permit compliance: training, BMP inspections, outfall screening, catch basin cleaning and street sweeping. Members stressed the need for a new DPW director before major planning and flagged a June 30 deadline to use remaining year-four consultant funds. A proposal to expand the task force from five to seven members was discussed and not pursued, and the meeting adjourned.

budget_items.topic: Regional stormwater coalition dues vs CEI training
budget_items.what_was_said: The town pays dues to the central Mass regional stormwater coalition, which provides training for any number of staff. This was compared with what CEI would charge for a one-off training.
CEI said its annual BMP inspection line is small relative to the whole MS4 allocation; inspections could later be brought in-house.
Possible funding named included town tax dollars, Chapter 90, stormwater funds to DPW, 319 grants, ARPA and MassWorks. The asset management grant was mentioned as in progress.
Speakers estimated the cost to buy and install a catch basin, excluding piping and engineering.

budget_items.topic: Catch basin cleaning equipment vs outsourcing
budget_items.what_was_said: The task force discussed new equipment or contracting out cleaning; a vac truck and per-basin vendor rates were estimated. Participants said the decision belongs with a new DPW director and the town manager.
figures_as_heard: a hundred dollars a catch basin

budget_items.what_was_said: Street sweeping miles dropped from the prior year. Contracting out sweeping was suggested to cost about as much as basin cleaning.
Money for a preliminary stormwater utility/GIS parcel analysis task must be used by June 30 or it returns to free cash. CEI needs a notice to proceed from the town.
The task force's charge includes establishing estimated cost and an ongoing funding source. A chair said they did not want to open a stormwater tax discussion yet.

decisions.decision: The DPW director will speak to the town's grant/administrative staff (Heather) about authorizing the parcel and structure analysis task before the June 30 deadline.
The proposal to expand the task force from five to seven members was not adopted; the group agreed to continue with liaisons attending unofficially.
The next meeting was set for 19 May.
CEI to return the BMP location data matched to street names; the town will look at training town staff for annual inspections once a new DPW director is in place.
CEI agreed to export its BMP evaluation checklist from GIS and share it with the town.

budget_items.topic: Recouping costs / revolving fund for stormwater
budget_items.what_was_said: Chair asked whether recouped costs from violations could go into a stormwater revolving account; staff said a revolving fund needs a specific purpose and revenue source and requires town meeting action.

budget_items.topic: Sewer/stormwater enterprise fund and utility fee
budget_items.what_was_said: Members said data on drains and maintenance is needed to make the case for an enterprise fund and utility fee that would be self-supporting.
Members discussed grants as a funding source, noting a prior 319 grant application was unsuccessful and that a defined project is needed first; a grant list was promised for the next meeting.

budget_items.topic: How current stormwater funds are determined
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion that DPW needs to track stormwater work and costs to support a future utility request, including administration, materials and an emergency accrual.
Chair asked whether stormwater fines could be directed to the stormwater utility fund; answer was that it would be looked into.

budget_items.topic: DPW budget line items for stormwater
budget_items.what_was_said: DPW head said there is a stormwater line item mainly for MS4 consultant compliance and a smaller drainage line, while catch basin cleaning sits in the highway budget; he will estimate total stormwater spending.
Members referenced a breakdown of reported stormwater spending out of a larger road/capital sum, including berms and catch basin work, as a basis for extrapolating annual capital work.
A member cited catch basin totals and the low number cleaned as justification for needing metrics before an enterprise fund can be argued.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force held no votes but agreed to set up a workshop for the planning board, conservation commission, DPW and building official on the stormwater process.
Members said drain and maintenance data is needed to make the case for a self-supporting stormwater enterprise fund and utility fee.
Staff said a stormwater revolving fund needs a specific purpose and revenue source and requires town meeting action; whether fines could go to a stormwater fund is to be looked into.
The DPW head said stormwater has its own budget line, mainly for MS4 consultant compliance, while catch basin cleaning sits in the highway budget; he will estimate total stormwater spending.
Follow-ups were assigned: a list of available grants, a website mockup, goals on the next agenda, and the consultant's scope of work shared with the group.

why_it_matters: Stormwater costs are spread across the DPW, highway and capital budgets, so the town's total spending on it is not visible in one place, which a future utility fee or enterprise fund would require.
Any revolving fund or utility fee would come to town meeting as a vote residents are asked to take, and the task force is collecting the data it would rest on.
watch_next: Next meeting on the third Thursday, the 17th: goals and objectives on the agenda, plus the grants list and website mockup.
DPW's estimate of total stormwater spending, and the date of the cross-board workshop, neither yet set in the minutes.

what_happened.line: The Stormwater Task Force took no budget action; it set goals, a regulatory workshop and requests for DPW spending history.
The DPW head is to provide past stormwater line-item spending and an estimate of stormwater costs across the budget.
Members discussed a stormwater enterprise fund or utility fee and agreed the need must be established first, before any fund is proposed.
The finance officer said a revolving fund for money recouped from developers needs a specific purpose and Town Meeting action.
The meeting opened short of a quorum, which was reached when Paula joined late, and the task force then approved two sets of minutes.

why_it_matters: A stormwater enterprise fund or utility fee would be a new charge on property owners, and any revolving fund would need a Town Meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on both later.
Stormwater costs are currently spread across a consulting line, a drainage line and the highway budget, so the DPW estimate is the first step toward seeing the whole cost in one place.
